title: Variables screen can create variants/groups that nothing can ever use — only ids 'color' and 'size' are consumed
detail: `onCreate` persists any variant the admin names: a direct-units variant or a group, with `id = unitId(name)` (VariablesTab.tsx:53-70), and `AddUnitsModal` happily saves units into it. But the ONLY consumer of `settings/variables` in the whole repo is the product form, which hardcodes the two ids it understands: `variables?.directUnits.find(d => d.id === 'color')` and `variables?.groups.find(g => g.id === 'size')` (admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:139-140), and writes only the `color`/`size` attribute keys (ProductFormPage.tsx:261). Grep confirms no other reader: web (`/home/h/barkath/web/src`), app (`/home/h/barkath/app/lib`) and functions never read `directUnits`/`groups` at all; the only other hits are the shared type and the seed. The seeded `material` group (scripts/seed.ts:168) is already unreachable data proving the point, and `GroupVariable.enabled` is written `true` at creation and never read or toggled anywhere.
failure_scenario: Admin opens Settings ▸ Variables ▸ Create variant, picks "Group (units inside)", types "Material", adds units Cotton/Linen/Silk, sees "Units saved". They then open a product to tag it as Cotton — the product form only renders Color and Size dropdowns, so Material never appears. The units sit in Firestore forever, unusable. Same for a colour variant named anything other than exactly "Color" (e.g. "Colour" → id `colour`): the swatches are saved but the product form's colour dropdown stays empty.
fix: Either drive the product form's variant dropdowns off the whole `directUnits`+`groups` arrays (render one Select per variable, key attributes by variable id) and honour `GroupVariable.enabled`, or lock the Variables screen down to editing units inside the two supported variables and remove the free-form Create-variant flow.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. VariablesTab.tsx:53-71 persists any admin-named direct variant or group (CreateVariantModal only blocks duplicate ids, and its own help text invites "Material"), and AddUnitsModal saves units into it with a "Units saved" toast. The sole consumer of settings/variables in the repo is ProductFormPage.tsx:139-140, which hardcodes d.id === 'color' and g.id === 'size', and writes only those two attribute keys (line 261), builds SKU/label from only those two (246, 249) and renders chips only for those two (445-446). Repo-wide grep: web/src, app/lib and functions/src contain zero references to directUnits/groups/attributes — customer surfaces show the pre-baked variant.label that admin composes from color+size names only; other hits are just packages/shared types, scripts/seed.ts and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts. The seeded 'material' group (seed.ts:168) is proof-by-example of unreachable data, and GroupVariable.enabled is written true and never read anywhere. No guard, fallback or server-side re-check exists (saveVariables is a plain setDoc merge). Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. The path is the screen's primary CTA (Create variant defaults to kind='group'). The design prototype shows a Material group on Variables yet only Color/Size columns on the product form, which supports the gap rather than excusing it. Additional reachable variant of the same bug: confirmDelete permits deleting the color/size entries when no unit is in use, and recreating them under any other spelling ("Colour" -> id 'colour') silently leaves the product form's dropdowns empty. Fixable either by constraining the create flow to the supported axes or by rendering a column per configured variant/group. Confidence medium only because one could argue two-axis variants are intended product scope — but even then the free-form create flow is a dead control that persists permanently unusable data.

title: category.productCount is written 0 on create and never maintained — web home shows "0 products" for every admin-created category
detail: `saveCategory` writes `productCount: 0` on create and never touches it again (there is no update path, no CF trigger, and `fanOutCategoryTint` doesn't touch it). The admin list papers over this by computing a live aggregation (CategoriesListPage.tsx:31-42) and falling back to the stored value only on failure. The web home tile reads the stored field directly: `web/src/components/home/CategoryCard.tsx:35` renders `{category.productCount === 1 ? '1 product' : `${category.productCount ?? 0} products`}`. The Flutter app already worked around it — `app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:63` literally comments "the stored `category.productCount` is never maintained by any Cloud Function (it's always 0)" and derives counts client-side. Only the seed masks it (scripts/seed.ts:293 hardcodes 3).
failure_scenario: Admin creates category "Prayer Mats", publishes 12 products into it. Admin's Categories list shows "12". The web home page tile for Prayer Mats shows "0 products" forever. Even the seeded categories drift: Perfumes permanently reads "3 products" no matter how many are added or deleted.
fix: Either stop writing/reading the denormalised field (drop it from the create payload and make web derive the count like the app does), or maintain it — increment/decrement in the product create/delete/category-reassign paths (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts) the same way `soldCount` is maintained.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:94 writes productCount:0 only on create; the update branch spreads `base` which omits the field, and setCategoryVisibility/updateSubCategories/fanOutCategoryTint never touch it. A grep of every write to the `categories` collection across admin/src, functions/src and scripts shows the only writers are those five calls plus the seed — functions/src has zero references to productCount and no Firestore trigger or scheduled sweep on categories. The consumer has no compute-on-read fallback: web/src/components/home/CategoryCard.tsx:35 renders the stored value directly and is live on the shop home (web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:99, top-4 tiles), so every admin-created category shows "0 products" permanently and seeded ones are frozen at 3. Admin's own list only hides it via a live aggregation (CategoriesListPage.tsx:31-42, stored value used only as ?? fallback at line 124), and app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:63 documents the same bug and works around it client-side. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Extra evidence the claim missed: the same rot is visible inside the admin panel for sub-categories — SubCategoriesPage.tsx:42 and CategoryFormPage.tsx:83 create subs with productCount:0, and SubCategoriesPage.tsx:131 renders {s.productCount ?? 0} raw with no aggregation (countSubCategoryProducts is used only for the delete guard at line 61), so that column is permanently 0. Fixable either by maintaining the denormalized field on product create/update/delete or by deriving counts on the web side as app and admin-list already do.

title: Tint fan-out writes to `products` — denied for a categories-only sub-admin, and its failure is reported as "Could not save the category" after the category already saved
detail: `fanOutCategoryTint` batch-updates `products/*` documents. firestore.rules:53-55 gates `products` writes on `canWrite('products')`, while the categories screens are gated on `canWrite('categories')` (rules line 49) — two independent module keys in MODULE_KEYS. In `CategoryFormPage.onSave` (CategoryFormPage.tsx:159-170) the fan-out runs inside the same try block *after* `saveCategory` has already committed, and the catch emits the blanket `toast.error('Could not save the category.')` without navigating. Nothing is rolled back and `initialTint` is never updated, so every retry re-enters the same failing path.
failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose permission matrix has Categories(edit) but not Products opens Perfumes, changes the tint, clicks Save changes. The category document IS updated (new tint on the category tile) but the batch on products throws PERMISSION_DENIED; the operator sees "Could not save the category.", stays on the form, and clicks Save again — same error, forever. Products keep the old tint, so product cards and the category tile disagree. Same misleading message hits a super-admin whenever the fan-out fails midway (>400 products = multiple batches; batch 2 failing leaves half the products on the old tint and reports a total failure).
fix: Run the fan-out only when the caller has products-write permission (or move it to a Cloud Function that checks the categories module and writes with admin credentials), and separate the toasts: report "Category saved, but product tints could not be updated" instead of "Could not save the category", and navigate/refresh `initialTint` so the retry is idempotent.

verdict.reason: Could not refute. Verified: firestore.rules:49 gates categories on canWrite('categories') while :50-57 gates products on canWrite('products'); MODULE_KEYS (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:253) treats them as independent, and SubAdminFormPage.toggleModule lets an operator enable Categories without Products, so the state is configurable. admin/src/app/router.tsx has no per-route module guard whatsoever (only RequireAuth), and Sidebar.tsx:12 surfaces Categories on categories.view, so the form and its unconditional Save button are reachable. No server-side fallback exists: there are zero Firestore triggers in functions/src, and functions/src/index.ts:15 explicitly states the categoryTint fan-out is a client-side batch by design. The field is live, not dead: web/src/components/product/ProductCard.tsx:37,72 renders product.categoryTint and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:83 snapshots it onto order lines. Code path confirmed at CategoryFormPage.tsx:159-170 — saveCategory commits, then fanOutCategoryTint runs in the same try, and one catch emits the blanket 'Could not save the category.' with no navigate; initialTint is only assigned in the mount effect (line 65) behind seededRef, so it never refreshes and every retry re-enters the failing branch. The 400-doc sequential loop in categories.ts:117-121 has no rollback, so a super-admin hitting a mid-loop failure gets half-migrated products plus a total-failure message. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists.

title: No Affiliate settings screen exists — settings/affiliate is read by 3 surfaces but writable by nobody
detail: `useAffiliate()` (settings.ts:25-27) is exported and never imported anywhere in admin/src — grep for `useAffiliate` returns only its own definition. `SETTINGS_TABS` (components/SettingsShell.tsx:22-28) lists only variables / delivery / gateway / storefront / support, and `SettingsPage.VALID` (routes/SettingsPage.tsx:13) has no 'affiliate' entry, so there is no route, chip or form for it. Yet `settings/affiliate` is read live by: functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:24-28 (`minWithdrawalPaise`, `processingFeeType`, `processingFeeValue`, `processingFeeMinPaise` — used at requests.ts:50-52 to compute the payout fee and reject under-minimum withdrawals), functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:41-42 (`defaultCommissionRate`), web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:55 + web/src/lib/affiliate.ts:40 (fee schedule shown to the customer), and app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_repository.dart:97. scripts/seed.ts:210-220 seeds all nine fields, so the values exist and silently govern real payouts. `commissionClearanceDays`, `maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise`, `enabled` and `shareMessage` are additionally never read by anything (functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:11 explicitly says clearance happens at delivery instead).
failure_scenario: An admin needs to raise the affiliate withdrawal minimum from ₹500 to ₹2,000 and add a 2% processing fee. They open Settings, cycle every tab (Variables, Delivery & tax, Payment gateway, Storefront, Support, plus the content-page chips) and find nothing for affiliates. The only way to change the value the requestWithdrawal callable enforces is to hand-edit the Firestore document in the Firebase console.
fix: Add an 'affiliate' tab to SETTINGS_TABS + SettingsPage.VALID with a form over settings/affiliate (minWithdrawalPaise, processingFeeType/Value/MinPaise, defaultCommissionRate as a percent input converted to a fraction, enabled), wired to a saveAffiliate() using the existing useAffiliate() hook. Drop commissionClearanceDays/maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise/shareMessage from the schema, or make a surface read them.

verdict.reason: Verified in full. admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25 exports useAffiliate() and nothing in admin/src imports it; there is no saveAffiliate writer, no 'affiliate' entry in SettingsShell.tsx:9-28 SETTINGS_TABS/SettingsTabId, and none in SettingsPage.tsx:13 VALID, so ?tab=affiliate silently falls back to Variables. admin/src/features/affiliate/ has only list + allocate pages, and grep for minWithdrawal|processingFee|defaultCommissionRate across admin/src returns zero hits — no surface writes settings/affiliate anywhere in the repo. The doc is nevertheless authoritative for money: functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:24-28 loads minWithdrawalPaise/processingFeeType/processingFeeValue/processingFeeMinPaise and uses them to compute processingFeePaise/netPayoutPaise and to hard-reject under-minimum withdrawals; functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:41-42 falls back to defaultCommissionRate; web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:55, web/src/lib/affiliate.ts and app/lib/.../affiliate_repository.dart:97 display the fee schedule; scripts/seed.ts:200-211 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:116 seed all nine fields. firebase/firestore.rules:56 already allows admin writes to settings/{docId}, so the gap is purely a missing admin form and is trivially fixable. The claim is not on the already-fixed list, and the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL note about manual affiliate payouts covers the absence of a bank-transfer API, not the absence of any way to configure the payout minimum/fee. Sub-claim also verified: commissionClearanceDays, maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise and shareMessage are referenced only by the shared type, the seeds, and a comment in functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:11.

title: Turning off "Online payment" in admin does not disable online payment in the Flutter app
detail: The admin writes `onlinePaymentEnabled` (PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:47) as an independent boolean. web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:161 honours it directly (`gateway?.onlinePaymentEnabled ?? true`). The app does not: app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:320 computes `final onlineEnabled = s.onlinePaymentEnabled || s.razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty;` — an OR against the key field. Because the Key ID field on the same admin card is almost always populated (scripts/seed.ts:185 writes 'rzp_test_XXXXXXXXXXXX'), the `|| razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty` branch keeps online payment permanently on in the app.
failure_scenario: Razorpay goes down, so the admin opens Payment gateway and toggles 'Online payment (UPI / cards / net-banking)' off, then saves. Web checkout correctly hides the online option. App customers still see and select 'Pay online', get pushed into the Razorpay sheet, and their orders fail — the admin's kill-switch appears to have worked because they only checked the website.
fix: Change app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:320 to `final onlineEnabled = s.onlinePaymentEnabled;` (matching web), or remove razorpayKeyId from the admin form entirely so the app has nothing to OR against.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real cross-surface defect. Admin writes onlinePaymentEnabled as an independent boolean (admin/src/features/settings/routes/PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:47, toggle at :136). Web honours it alone: web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:238 `const onlineEnabled = gateway?.onlinePaymentEnabled ?? true;`. The Flutter app instead ORs it with the key field: app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:424 `final onlineEnabled = s.onlinePaymentEnabled || s.razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty;` — so with a populated Key ID (scripts/seed.ts:185 'rzp_test_XXXXXXXXXXXX', and any live install) the admin kill-switch is inert in the app: the Razorpay tile still renders (line 490) and the draft can even be auto-switched TO 'razorpay' (lines 440-442). No rescue elsewhere: app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:208-209 parses both fields correctly with the intended `?? true` web-mirroring default (comment at 204-206 says exactly that), and there is no server-side re-check — grep for onlinePaymentEnabled/codEnabled/paymentGateway across functions/src returns nothing and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:418 accepts z.enum(['cod','razorpay']) without consulting settings/paymentGateway. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists (Razorpay test-mode note concerns money flow, not the availability toggle). Only defect in the report is stale line numbers: the app expression is at :424 (claim said :320) and the web read at :238 (claim said :161); the code text quoted is exact. Fixable in one line (use && or drop the OR).

title: COD / wallet / online toggles and the COD cap are enforced only in the clients — placeOrder ignores settings/paymentGateway
detail: The four controls on this card (`codEnabled` :110, `codMaxAmountPaise` :121, `walletEnabled` :133, `onlinePaymentEnabled` :136) are written to settings/paymentGateway and then read *only* by the two clients (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:158-174, app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:317-321) to hide radio buttons. `grep -rn "paymentGateway" functions/src` returns zero hits: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts never loads the doc. Its placeOrder schema is `paymentMethod: z.enum(['cod','razorpay'])` (checkout.ts:393) and `summarise()` (checkout.ts:335-363) reads only settings/delivery and settings/tax; it adds `delivery.codSurchargePaise` for any 'cod' order (checkout.ts:349) and accepts any `useWallet` amount. So none of the four settings is a real switch.
failure_scenario: COD fraud spikes, so the admin turns 'Cash on delivery' off and saves. Customers on an already-open app/web tab (their client still holds the previous settings snapshot for the life of the screen), or anyone calling the placeOrder callable directly, keep placing COD orders successfully — the server accepts them, prices in the COD surcharge, and they land in the Orders list as normal. The same applies to a ₹5,000 COD cap: a ₹40,000 COD order placed from a stale client is accepted.
fix: Load settings/paymentGateway inside placeOrder and reject with failed-precondition when `paymentMethod === 'cod' && !codEnabled`, when `codMaxAmountPaise > 0 && subtotalPaise > codMaxAmountPaise`, when `paymentMethod === 'razorpay' && !onlinePaymentEnabled`, and when wallet is used while `walletEnabled === false`.

verdict.reason: Could not refute. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts reads only settings/delivery and settings/tax (lines 464-465); repo-wide grep for paymentGateway/codEnabled/codMaxAmountPaise/onlinePaymentEnabled across functions/src and firebase/*.rules returns zero hits (the sole walletEnabled hit is an unrelated affiliate field in functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:27). PlaceOrderSchema (checkout.ts:418) accepts paymentMethod 'cod' unconditionally and summarise() (checkout.ts:354, 369) prices in delivery.codSurchargePaise for any COD order with no enable/cap check. The doc is written by admin/src/features/settings/routes/PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:44-47 and read only by the two clients for UI gating (web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:46 + web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:235-251; app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:187,202-208), both defaulting absent flags to true. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and placeOrder already reads two other settings docs so the fix is the established pattern. One minor inaccuracy that does not change the verdict: useWallet is a boolean and the server reads the real wallet balance inside the transaction, so wallet spend is capped at the true balance — only the walletEnabled toggle itself is unenforced. The COD-off and COD-cap bypasses are real and reachable by any authenticated customer calling placeOrder directly or from a stale client tab.

title: "Create variant" builds variants no screen can ever use — only ids 'color' and 'size' are consumed
detail: The Variables tab lets an admin create arbitrary direct-unit variants and groups (VariablesTab.tsx:53-71 → variables.ts:38-52 writes settings/variables.directUnits/groups) and add units to each. But settings/variables has exactly one consumer in the entire monorepo: admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:139-141, which hardcodes `directUnits.find(d => d.id === 'color')` and `groups.find(g => g.id === 'size')`. Nothing in web/src, app/lib or functions/src reads settings/variables at all (verified by grep for 'settings/variables' and 'directUnits'). The product form persists only those two keys — `attributes: { ...r.attrs, color, size }` (ProductFormPage.tsx:261). The seeded 'material' group (scripts/seed.ts:167-176) with Cotton/Silk/Linen is already dead for exactly this reason. CreateVariantModal also blocks a duplicate id (CreateVariantModal.tsx:37), so the only usable variants are the two that already exist.
failure_scenario: An admin clicks 'Create variant', picks 'Group (units inside)', names it 'Fragrance strength', adds units Light/Medium/Strong and saves — every step shows a success toast and the group renders in the Variables tab. They then open Products → New and find only Color and Size dropdowns; the new variant is unusable and invisible to web, app and every order/invoice.
fix: Either drive the product form's variant axes off settings/variables generically (iterate directUnits + enabled groups instead of hardcoding 'color'/'size'), or restrict the Variables tab to editing the two supported variants and remove the Create-variant flow.

verdict.reason: Verified as a genuine dead control. VariablesTab.tsx:53-71 lets an admin create an arbitrarily-named direct-unit variant or group and persists it to settings/variables (admin/src/features/settings/api/variables.ts:43-46), and firestore.rules:56 permits the write, so the flow completes with success toasts and the new variant renders in the tab. But settings/variables has exactly one consumer in the monorepo — ProductFormPage.tsx:139-140 — which hardcodes directUnits.find(d => d.id === 'color') and groups.find(g => g.id === 'size'); the variant-row table renders only two MiniSelects (lines 468, 472) with no map over groups, and the save writes only those two keys (line 261, where r.attrs is mere carry-over since line 49 strips color/size on load). Grep confirms no reader of settings/variables, directUnits, or variant attributes anywhere in web/src, app/lib, functions/src or packages/shared runtime code; customer surfaces resolve variants by id/label/sku (e.g. app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:169-173). The seeded 'material' group (scripts/seed.ts:167-176 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts) is already inert, which is concrete evidence rather than a hypothetical. No guard, fallback, or server-side re-check mitigates it, and it is not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. It is fixable either by rendering one column per enabled group in the product form or by constraining the Create-variant control. One narrowing nuance: the control is not entirely useless — a variant named exactly 'Color' or 'Size' produces the consumed ids, so it retains a recreate-after-delete purpose; that limits severity but does not refute the defect.

title: GST rate is rounded to a whole percent on load, so any save of the Delivery & Tax tab silently rewrites a fractional rate
detail: The form seeds the input with `setGstPercent(String(Math.round((t.gstRate ?? 0) * 100)))` (DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:57) and saves it back with `gstRate: (Number(gstPercent) || 0) / 100` (line 88). The round-trip is lossy for any non-integer percent — 0.125 → '13' → 0.13, 0.025 → '3' → 0.03. There is also no range validation: any number is accepted, so '18' typed as a fraction ('0.18') writes gstRate 0.0018 and '1800' writes 18. gstRate is consumed as a fraction by functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:351 (`Math.round(net * Number(tax.gstRate ?? 0))`), web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:119 and app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:210, so the value directly sets the tax charged on every order. Note that a single 'Save changes' button writes both settings/delivery and settings/tax (lines 77-97), so an unrelated edit triggers the rewrite.
failure_scenario: GST is 12.5% (gstRate 0.125 in Firestore). The admin opens Delivery & tax only to change the standard delivery fee from ₹49 to ₹59. The GST field renders '13'. They click Save changes and the tax rate is silently rewritten to 0.13 — every subsequent order is taxed 13% instead of 12.5%, with nothing in the UI indicating a tax change was made.
fix: Seed with the exact value (`String(+( (t.gstRate ?? 0) * 100 ).toFixed(2))`) instead of Math.round, and validate on save that the entered percent is a finite number in 0–100 before dividing by 100.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect. DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:57 seeds the GST field with Math.round(gstRate*100) while line 88 saves (Number(gstPercent)||0)/100, and the underlying Field component (admin/src/features/settings/components/fields.tsx) is a bare <input type="number" inputMode="decimal"> with no step/min/max and no onChange sanitiser — so the same form that persists 12.5 -> 0.125 will render it as '13' and rewrite it to 0.13 on any later save. The defect is reachable entirely through this one screen; no external writer is needed. No guard exists elsewhere: a repo-wide grep for gstRate finds only the shared type (unconstrained `number`), the 0.18 defaults in settings.ts/seed.ts/bootstrap-real.ts, and three consumers that use the stored fraction raw with no clamping or re-derivation (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:371 `Math.round(net * Number(tax.gstRate ?? 0))`, web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:119, app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:201/231). packages/shared/src/money.ts:58 inclusiveTaxPaise takes a percent but has zero call sites, so there is no alternate path that makes the rounding benign. The single 'Save changes' button does write settings/delivery and settings/tax together (lines 77-97), so an unrelated delivery-fee edit does trigger the tax rewrite. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. Severity is moderated by two facts: the checkout tax term only applies when gstEnabled && !pricesIncludeTax (defaults have pricesIncludeTax: true), and Indian GST slabs are usually whole percents — but 1.5% and 0.25% rates would be silently rewritten to 2% and 0%, and the missing range validation ('0.18' -> 0.0018, '1800' -> 1800%) is unguarded on every surface. Confidence medium rather than high only because of the real-world rarity of fractional GST rates, not because of any doubt about the mechanism.

title: Sub-category Hide/Show toggle is dead on the Flutter app — the app model drops `visibility`
detail: `toggle()` flips `visibility` inside the embedded `subCategories` array and persists it via `updateSubCategories`. The web honours it (`web/src/components/catalog/CategoriesView.tsx:50-52` and `ListingView.tsx:52-53` filter on `s.visibility === 'visible'`). The Flutter app does not: `app/lib/features/catalog/data/category.dart:31-36` builds `SubCategory` with only `slug` and `name` — the class has no visibility field at all (category.dart:3-7) — and `app/lib/features/catalog/category_products_screen.dart:122-123` renders a chip for every entry in `_subs`. Note also that on both surfaces hiding a sub only removes the filter chip; the products still list under "All".
failure_scenario: Admin hides the "EDP" sub-category of Perfumes because the line is discontinued. On the website the EDP facet disappears as expected. In the app, the EDP chip is still on the category screen and still filters to those products — so the merchandising decision silently applies to one storefront only.
fix: Parse and filter `visibility` in `app/lib/features/catalog/data/category.dart` (mirror the web's `!= 'hidden'` convention), and decide one behaviour for the products themselves: either exclude products whose `subCategorySlug` points at a hidden sub from the listing on both surfaces, or relabel the toggle so it clearly only controls the filter chip.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all surfaces. Admin (admin/src/features/categories/routes/SubCategoriesPage.tsx:50-56) persists sub-category `visibility` into the embedded `subCategories` array; web honours it (web/src/components/catalog/CategoriesView.tsx:50-52 and ListingView.tsx:52-53 filter `s.visibility === 'visible'`); the Flutter app does not — app/lib/features/catalog/data/category.dart:3-7 declares `SubCategory` with only `slug` and `name`, and `Category.fromDoc` (lines 31-37) drops `visibility` entirely, so category_products_screen.dart:48,122-123 renders a chip for every entry. Refutation attempts failed: grep of `visibility` across app/lib yields only product-level and category-level filters (catalog_repository.dart:28,54,74,88,135,163; checkout_repository.dart:144) — none inspects the sub-category array; the app reads categories directly from Firestore with no Cloud Function re-check; `subCategories` appears nowhere else in app/lib; and this is not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Severity is moderate rather than high because, as the claim itself notes, hiding a sub only removes the facet/chip on either surface (products remain listed under "All"), so it is a merchandising inconsistency, not data exposure — but the admin toggle is genuinely inert on the app and the fix is trivial (add `visibility` to the Dart model and filter `_subs`).

title: slugify() can return an empty string — category save fails with an opaque error and sub-categories/units save with empty ids
detail: `slugify` strips everything outside `[a-z0-9]`, so a name written in Arabic/Urdu/Hindi (or pure punctuation) yields `''`. `saveCategory` then calls `setDoc(doc(db, 'categories', ''), …)` (categories.ts:89), which the Firestore SDK rejects synchronously; `CategoryFormPage.onSave` catches it and shows only `'Could not save the category.'` (CategoryFormPage.tsx:166-168). The name field itself only validates non-empty (CategoryFormPage.tsx:136). The sub-category paths are worse — they don't hit a doc path so nothing throws: `SubCategoriesPage.add` (line 42) and `CategoryFormPage.addSub` (line 83) persist `{ id: '', slug: '', name: 'عطور' }` into the array. The same hole exists in `unitId` (settings/api/variables.ts:25) used by CreateVariantModal and AddUnitsModal. Also, image upload on a new category with such a name hits the `if (!catId)` branch and tells the admin to "Enter the category name first" when they already have (CategoryFormPage.tsx:115-118).
failure_scenario: Admin (this is an Islamic store) types "عطور" as a category name and clicks Save category → "Could not save the category." with no hint what is wrong; it will never succeed. On the sub-category screen the same name is accepted: a sub with `slug: ''` is stored, appears in the product form's Sub-category dropdown with value `''`, and selecting it then fails product validation with "Sub-category is required." A second non-latin sub is refused as a duplicate because both slugify to `''`.
fix: Validate the derived slug before writing: if `slugify(name) === ''`, reject with a specific message ("Use at least one Latin letter or digit in the name") in CategoryFormPage, SubCategoriesPage, CreateVariantModal and AddUnitsModal — or fall back to a transliteration/random id and keep the display name as typed.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end; could not refute any link. (1) slugify (admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:31) returns '' for any name with no [a-z0-9] chars — confirmed by running the exact regex on 'عطور', 'इत्र', '&&&'. (2) Category create really fails: categories.ts:89 does setDoc(doc(db,'categories','')); in the installed @firebase/firestore 4.7.3, ResourcePath.fromString drops zero-length segments leaving ['categories'], and __PRIVATE_validateDocumentPath throws 'must have an even number of segments'. The throw is swallowed by the bare catch at CategoryFormPage.tsx:166-168 → generic 'Could not save the category.' The only name validation is !name.trim() (line 136), and the duplicate guard (line 143) can't help since no slug:'' category can ever exist. (3) Sub-categories are worse and silent: SubCategoriesPage.add:42 and CategoryFormPage.addSub:83 push {id:'',slug:'',name:…} into the embedded array; no doc path is involved so nothing throws. There is no server-side re-check — firebase/firestore.rules:49 is `allow write: if canWrite('categories')`, permission-only with zero content validation, and no Cloud Function touches category writes (correct per the architecture rules, so the client is the only place this can be fixed). (4) Downstream breakage confirmed: ProductFormPage.tsx:346 maps options to {value: s.slug}, so the empty-slug sub is selectable as '' and ProductFormPage.tsx:169 then fails with 'Sub-category is required.'; a second non-latin sub is refused as a duplicate because both slugify to ''. (5) The unitId twin (settings/api/variables.ts:25) is the identical regex feeding makeColorUnit/makeGroupUnit id fields — notably unitCode two lines below DOES have an `|| 'X'` empty fallback, showing the gap is an oversight rather than a convention. (6) The image-upload complaint is accurate (CategoryFormPage.tsx:114-118 tells the admin to enter a name they already entered). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; realistic input for an Islamic perfume store; small local fix (fallback slug + form-level validation message).

title: Variant units can never be edited — a wrong colour hex or a typo'd name is permanent once a product uses it
detail: AddUnitsModal only supports add and remove. Re-adding a unit with the same name is refused (`if (units.some(u => u.id === id))` line 53-56, and the id is derived from the name), and removing a unit that any product references is blocked by the delete-safety check (line 76-81, and VariablesTab.tsx:99-115 for the chip on the card). There is no rename input, no hex re-picker on an existing chip, and no edit affordance anywhere on VariablesTab — the chip only carries a remove button (VariablesTab.tsx:142-150). `hex` is stored per unit (`ColorUnit.hex`) and used to paint the swatch in the product form (ProductFormPage.tsx:143, 467).
failure_scenario: Admin adds colour "Ivory" and mis-picks the swatch as black. Three products are saved with variant attribute `color: ivory`. They return to Settings ▸ Variables to fix the swatch: the chip has only an ✕, clicking it says "In use by 3 products — cannot remove", and adding "Ivory" again in the modal says "That unit already exists." The wrong swatch is now permanent unless someone edits Firestore by hand.
fix: Make the unit chips editable — click a chip to reopen name/hex in the modal, writing back the same `id` (rename changes only `name`, never the id, so product attributes stay valid). Re-derive `code` on rename with the same collision check.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at every cited line. AddUnitsModal.tsx only supports add (lines 49-67, duplicate id refused because unitId() is name-derived) and remove (69-88, blocked when countProductsUsingUnit > 0); existing chips at 150-175 render a static swatch and an ✕ only — no name field, no color re-picker, no click-to-edit. VariablesTab.tsx's chip() (142-150) likewise exposes only onDel, and its delete-safety guards (99-115, 118-134) block removal of in-use units. Refutation attempts failed: saveVariables (api/variables.ts:38) has exactly one caller file, the updateSettingsVariables callable referenced in functions/src/index.ts:73 does not exist (functions/src/catalog/ has only inventory.ts), and web/ and app/ never read settings/variables, so there is no other surface, no server-side re-check, and no fallback. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. One nuance: hex itself is admin-only cosmetics (consumed just by ProductFormPage.tsx:143/467), and a tedious workaround exists (clear the attribute on referencing products, delete, re-add the same name — the id regenerates identically), so "permanent unless someone edits Firestore" is overstated. But the same missing update path makes the unit NAME uncorrectable, and names are functional: ProductFormPage.tsx:249 snapshots them into variant.label (customer-facing on web ProductDetail.tsx:128 and app product_details_screen.dart:433) and unitCode(name) feeds the SKU at line 246. So it is a real, fixable broken-CRUD defect; a fix must keep the unit id stable on rename since products reference it.

title: Categories list re-runs one count query per category on every snapshot and swallows failures silently
detail: The effect depends on `[categories]`, which is a brand-new array reference on every Firestore snapshot from `useLiveCollection` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts maps `snap.docs` fresh each time). So every write to any category document — hiding one, deleting one, another admin's edit, or the initial listener settle — refires N `getCountFromServer` aggregation queries (categories.ts:41-46). The whole chain ends in `.catch(() => undefined)` (line 38), so a permission or network failure leaves `counts` empty with no error surfaced; the column silently falls back to `c.productCount ?? 0` (line 124), which is always 0 for admin-created categories.
failure_scenario: With 12 categories, an admin toggling Hide on one category fires 12 aggregation queries; toggling five categories in a row fires 60. If any of those reject (offline, backend hiccup), the Products column silently shows 0 for every category and the operator believes the catalogue is empty — then hits "reassign them first" when they try to delete, with no clue why the two numbers disagree.
fix: Key the effect on a stable value (e.g. `categories.map(c => c.id).join(',')`), and surface failures — set an error flag and render "—" with a retry rather than the misleading 0.

verdict.reason: Claim holds on every checkable point. useLiveCollection (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts) rebuilds the array via snap.docs.map on each snapshot, so the effect at CategoriesListPage.tsx:31-42, keyed on [categories], refires N getCountFromServer aggregation queries per category snapshot — in fact ~2N per admin write, since an updateDoc with serverTimestamp yields both an optimistic and a server-ack snapshot. emit() clones only the snapshot wrapper (data reference preserved), so unrelated re-renders do not refire, but any category write does. The .catch(() => undefined) at line 38 swallows every failure with no error state, and the fallback c.productCount ?? 0 at line 124 is confirmed always 0: saveCategory writes productCount: 0 at creation (categories.ts:94) and no Cloud Function ever maintains it — app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:63 states this outright ("never maintained by any Cloud Function (it's always 0)"); only scripts/seed.ts writes non-zero. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and no memoization, cache, or guard exists. Severity is lower than the report implies: the destructive path is independently guarded — askDelete (line 52) re-fetches the count server-side before opening the confirm dialog, so an empty counts map cannot cause an accidental delete, and N is small (seed has 4 categories). But redundant network round-trips plus a silently-wrong 0 in the Products column is a real, two-line-fixable defect, not a cosmetic one.

title: Sub-categories screen shows a Products column that nothing ever writes — always 0
detail: The table renders `{s.productCount ?? 0}`. `SubCategory.productCount` is written as the literal `0` when a sub is created — SubCategoriesPage.tsx:42 and CategoryFormPage.tsx:83 — and no code path in admin, web, app, functions or the scheduled sweeps ever updates it (grep for `productCount` returns only these writers plus the seed's hardcoded 1). Meanwhile the delete-safety guard right below it computes the real number with `countSubCategoryProducts` (categories.ts:49-58), so the screen already has access to the truth and doesn't use it.
failure_scenario: Admin opens Perfumes ▸ sub-categories to decide which sub to retire. Every row shows "1" (seeded value) or "0" (anything they created), regardless of the 40 products actually attached. They click ✕ on a sub showing 0 and get "Oud has 12 products — reassign them first" — the column flatly contradicts the guard.
fix: Populate the column from `countSubCategoryProducts` (one aggregation per sub on mount, or one grouped pass over the category's products) and stop persisting the dead `productCount: 0` field on the embedded objects.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. Repo-wide grep for `productCount` (admin, web, app, functions, packages/shared, scripts, no node_modules) finds only: the two type declarations (packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts:11,26), three literal-`0` initializers (SubCategoriesPage.tsx:42, CategoryFormPage.tsx:83, categories.ts:94), hardcoded seed values (scripts/seed.ts:293,300; add-back-to-school.ts:72,79), and three reads. No Cloud Function, trigger, sweep, or Flutter/web code ever updates SubCategory.productCount when a product is created, deleted, or reassigned, so the value is frozen at its creation-time literal. The sibling screen proves the intended pattern and shows this one is the outlier: CategoriesListPage.tsx:30-42 runs a getCountFromServer aggregation effect and renders `counts[c.id] ?? c.productCount ?? 0`, explicitly demoting the stale field to a fallback with the comment "Live product counts via aggregation (no denormalization trigger needed)". SubCategoriesPage.tsx:131 renders the bare `s.productCount ?? 0` with no such effect. The correct value is already reachable in-file: countSubCategoryProducts (admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:49-58) is imported at line 11 and used by askDelete at line 61, and products genuinely carry subCategoryId (packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts:63, seed.ts:355), so the guard's "N products — reassign them first" toast will contradict a column reading 0. Not covered by the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists; the path is reachable via /categories/:id/sub. Only inaccuracy is the title's "always 0" — seeded subs render the hardcoded 1 — which the claim body already concedes and which does not affect the defect.

title: Content pages missing an `order` field are invisible in the settings rail and can never be edited
detail: `useContentPages()` queries `query(collection(db,'content'), orderBy('order','asc'))` (content.ts:24-26). Firestore excludes documents that lack the orderBy field, so any content doc without `order` never appears. scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:121-124 — the script used to bootstrap the real project — writes `content/privacyPolicy` and `content/termsConditions` with only `{id, title, body, bodyHtml, version, lastEditorUid, publishedAt, updatedAt}`: no `order`, no `slug`, no `published`, no `sections`, no `system`. The rail in SettingsShell.tsx:99-118 renders from that same query, and SettingsPage.tsx:44-46 resolves `?tab=content&id=…` against it, falling back to `pages[0]` and then to `<VariablesTab/>` (SettingsPage.tsx:65-74) when the list is empty. There is no unordered fallback and no 'no pages' empty state.
failure_scenario: On the real (bootstrapped, non-seeded) project an admin opens Settings to edit the Privacy policy. The chip rail shows only the five built-in tabs and '+ New page'; clicking a bookmarked /settings?tab=privacy silently renders the Variables tab. The two existing content docs are unreachable and un-editable from the admin, and the storefront also hides them (`published` is missing → falsy). The admin's only recourse is to create duplicate pages.
fix: Query the collection unordered and sort by `(order ?? 0)` client-side (the web already sorts in memory — web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:66-75), and/or backfill order/slug/published/sections in bootstrap-real.ts.

verdict.reason: Confirmed; I could not refute it. admin/src/features/settings/api/content.ts:23-27 uses query(collection(db,'content'), orderBy('order','asc')), and Firestore silently omits docs lacking the orderBy field. The repo's own production bootstrap — scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:121-124, wired as scripts/package.json "bootstrap": "tsx bootstrap-real.ts" and called from seedSettings()/main(), targeting the real project barkath-25607 — writes content/privacyPolicy and content/termsConditions with only {id,title,body,bodyHtml,version,lastEditorUid,publishedAt,updatedAt}: no order, slug, published, sections or system. scripts/seed.ts:232-258 does write the full schema but is emulator-only (FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST guardrail), which is why the bug never appears in dev/e2e. No fallback exists in admin: SettingsShell.tsx:99-118 renders the rail straight from that list, and SettingsPage.tsx:44-46 resolves ?id= only via pages.find(p => p.id === requestedId), falling back to pages[0] and then to <VariablesTab/> (SettingsPage.tsx:64-74), so an absent doc can never reach <ContentPageTab/> even though useContentPage(docId) would fetch it by id; the legacy map privacy→privacyPolicy / terms→termsConditions (SettingsPage.tsx:19-22) points at exactly those two docs, so those bookmarks render Variables. Decisive corroboration that admin is the outlier: both other surfaces deliberately avoid orderBy and sort in memory with a missing-field tolerance — web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:73-80 sorts with (a.order ?? 0), and app/lib/features/settings/data/content_repository.dart:15-23 sorts in memory "matching the web". No backfill/migration script exists (scripts/ contains only backfill-return-item-status.mjs, unrelated), useLiveCollection (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts) has no unordered retry, and nothing on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists covers content pages. Severity caveat: impact is bounded — the admin can still create fresh pages (createContentPage always writes order/slug/published, and web resolves by slug), so the harm is two permanently unreachable orphan docs plus dead legacy bookmarks rather than a broken storefront. Still a real, functional, one-line-fixable defect (drop the orderBy and sort client-side like web/app; also complete the bootstrap write).

title: Tax form writes businessCity, businessCountry and hsnCodes that no surface reads
detail: DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:152-153 renders 'Business city' and 'Business country' inputs and line 92-93 writes `businessCity` / `businessCountry` to settings/tax; line 95 also round-trips `hsnCodes`. Grepping all four surfaces, `businessCity` and `businessCountry` appear only in packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:60-61, scripts/seed.ts:196-197 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:115 — no read in web/src, app/lib, functions/src or anywhere else in admin/src. `hsnCodes` is the same (types + seed only) and has no editor at all, so it is preserved forever but never editable and never rendered. By contrast the sibling fields on the same card ARE read: `legalName` and `gstin` by app/lib/features/orders/orders_repository.dart:43-47 (invoice issuer), `gstRate`/`gstEnabled`/`pricesIncludeTax` by all three checkout paths.
failure_scenario: An admin relocates the business, updates 'Business city' from Bengaluru to Chennai and saves. Nothing changes on the invoices in the app, the web account pages, or any export — the invoice issuer line only prints legalName + GSTIN. The admin believes the address on customer invoices has been corrected.
fix: Either surface businessCity/businessCountry on the invoice issuer block (app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:116-117 and the web equivalent) alongside legalName/gstin, or remove the two inputs and the hsnCodes field from the schema.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. admin/src/features/settings/routes/DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:152-153 renders editable 'Business city'/'Business country' fields and lines 92-93 persist them to settings/tax, but an exhaustive grep across functions/src, web/src, app/lib, admin/src and packages/shared finds no reader: the only hits are the type (packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:60-61), DEFAULT_TAX (admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:119-120), scripts/seed.ts:196-197 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:115. Each settings/tax consumer was checked individually — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:465, web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:45 and app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:186 read only gstRate/gstEnabled/pricesIncludeTax; app/lib/features/orders/data/orders_repository.dart:43-53 fetchIssuer() returns only legalName+gstin and app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:147-148 prints just 'name · GSTIN'. The server invoice (functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:52-64) doesn't read settings/tax at all — it hardcodes the BARAKATH header and prints only the customer's Bill-to address. So the failure scenario holds: an admin editing Business city sees no change on any invoice or export. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Caveat on scope: the hsnCodes half of the report is weak — the `hsnCodes: tax?.hsnCodes ?? {}` round-trip is correct preservation (saveTax uses merge:true), and the missing editor is a feature gap, not a defect; the real, fixable issue is the two dead admin inputs, which should either be removed or wired into the invoice issuer.
